item.title: Overwhelmed by To-Do Lists? The Monday Call Question
item.description: Monday, 9:05, a client asks what your priorities are this week, and your head fills with twenty things. A quiet story about a simpler planner.

item.title: Am I Losing Money on My Handmade Products After Fees?
item.description: Your bestseller sells every week, but after fees, postage and materials you can't say what's left. A quiet Sunday at the craft fair, and a calmer way to look.

item.title: Applied to So Many Jobs? The Family Brunch Question
item.description: Someone asks, 'Have you heard back?' and you can't say which companies you even wrote to. A calm story about job applications and finding your footing.

item.title: Backup Drive Full? The Bakery Question at 6:30 am
item.description: The owner asks, 'We're backed up, right?' and the drive says otherwise. A calm story about backups, old logs and finally trusting them.

item.title: Best Seller Keeps Selling Out? The Key Kiosk and the Blue Mug
item.description: Your best seller is gone again and the messages are getting shorter. A quiet story about the stock you never saw running out, and what a calm Monday looks like.

item.title: Rewriting Data Scripts Again? The Cottage Week Off
item.description: A week off that isn't one: the same CSV cleanup, rewritten from scratch on a cottage sofa. A story for developers tired of rebuilding old scripts.

item.title: Excel Trackers Scattered? The Climbing Gym Café Lunch
item.description: Invoices in one file, hours in another, quotes somewhere else. A quiet lunch story about what changes when your freelance Excel trackers live in one place.

item.title: No Planner Fits Your Freelance Year? The Stationery Aisle
item.description: Three diaries in your hands, none made for freelancers. A short story about finding one calm place for your year, your clients and your invoices.

item.title: Can't Remember Which Clients Paid You? The MOT Waiting Room
item.description: A client asks if you got their payment, and you honestly don't know. A quiet story about losing track of who paid, and what it feels like to know again.

item.title: New Client Onboarding Chaos? The Reception Chair at 9:50
item.description: You're in a new client's lobby with the scope scattered across three emails and half the logins missing. A calmer way to begin every project.

item.title: Client Says They Paid, But You Can't Find It? The Ferry Terminal
item.description: The client swears the money went out last week. Your bank shows nothing, and two invoices look alike. A calm story about untangling a payment mix-up.

item.title: Client Wants More Revisions Than Agreed? The Pottery Class Pause
item.description: Round four of 'just one small change' arrives mid-lunch. A quiet story about saying no to extra revisions politely, without losing the client or your calm.

item.title: CSV Full of Duplicates Every Week? The Friday 11:00 Call
item.description: Same export, same duplicates, same odd formatting every week. A story about the Friday call where the numbers didn't match, and a calmer way to start the week.

item.title: Customers Order Things You No Longer Have? The Parcel Locker Queue
item.description: Wednesday, 8:10 am, parcel queue: another order for a tin you sold out of. A calm story about stock surprises, and what it feels like when they stop.

item.title: Do I Charge Enough as a Freelancer? The Plumber at the Kitchen Door
item.description: A plumber hands over a bill without flinching, and a freelancer wonders why she can't do the same. A quiet story about charging enough and feeling paid.

item.title: Does My Hourly Rate Cover Taxes and Unpaid Time? The Bus Home
item.description: On the bus home, a nice number on an invoice suddenly feels too small. A quiet story about rates, taxes and the hours nobody pays you for.

item.title: Double Billed a Client by Accident? The Monday Phone Call
item.description: You sent the same invoice twice and the client noticed first. A quiet story about the sinking feeling, and what a calmer way to keep track feels like.

item.title: Invoices and Hours in Separate Files? The EV Charger Wait
item.description: Thirty-eight minutes at a charger, invoices in one file and hours in another. A freelancer story about finally seeing it all in one place.

item.title: Craft Stock and Orders in a Mess? The Courier Slot
item.description: Monday, 7:50 am, the courier comes at nine and you can't tell which orders are late or what you still have in stock. A calm story for craft sellers.

item.title: Need More Time on a Client Project? The Bank Holiday Kitchen Table
item.description: The deadline is Friday and the work won't be ready. You're at your parents' kitchen table, rewriting one sentence to a client. A calmer way through.

item.title: Sent an Invoice Weeks Ago, Not Sure They Paid? One Bar of Signal
item.description: You're on a cottage porch with one bar of signal and can't remember if that invoice from weeks ago was ever paid. A calm story about not having to guess.

item.title: Lost Track of Job Applications? The Bookshop Call
item.description: A recruiter calls and you can't remember which role she means. A calm story about job applications, follow-ups and interview prep that stops living in your head.

item.title: Keep Running Out of Stock? The Vet Waiting Room Message
item.description: The cat is in the vet's back room when a customer writes that your bestseller is gone again. A calm story for small shop owners tired of finding out too late.

item.title: Chasing Late Payment Feels Like Begging? The Gate at 7:40
item.description: You're standing at the school gate, thumb over 'send', and the reminder still isn't written. A quiet story about chasing money without feeling like you're begging.

item.title: Client Never Paid the Final Balance After Your Shoot? The Gallery Link
item.description: The gallery is delivered, the thank-you came, the final balance didn't. A photographer's quiet Thursday at the print shop, and what makes it easier.

item.title: Forgot the Balance After a Wedding Shoot? The Physio Corridor
item.description: Three months after the wedding, a tagged photo reminds you: the final balance was never chased. A calm story for photographers, and what changes after.

item.title: Server Disk Full Again? Old Log Files and a 7:45 Client Call
item.description: The disk is full again, and the culprit is months of old log files. A calm story about the Monday it stopped happening, and what changed.

item.title: Small Business AI Prompts: The Job Ad You Kept Postponing
item.description: Tuesday, 14:10, the shop is quiet and the job ad is still a blinking cursor. A story for owners who lose hours to blank pages. Prompts that fill in.

item.title: Shop Keeps Overselling Stock? The Wedding Pew Buzz
item.description: Your phone buzzes mid-vows: another order for something you no longer have. A calm story for small shop owners tired of overselling and apologising.

item.title: Keep Selling Items You Don't Have? The Cinema Foyer
item.description: The trailers are rolling when your phone buzzes: another order for the last skein, sold twice. A quiet story for shop owners who keep overselling.

item.title: Afraid to Tell Clients Your Freelance Rate? The Lift to Floor 4
item.description: You typed the number, deleted it, typed a smaller one. A quiet story about the fear of saying your freelance rate out loud, and what calms it.

item.title: Agency Paid Late Again? A Translator's Quiet Tuesday Lunch
item.description: The agency invoice is 60 days old and you can't find the right words. A translator's lunch-break story about chasing late payment without the knot.

item.title: Can't Find Your Old Data Scripts? The Canteen Queue Ping
item.description: You know you wrote that cleanup script once. Somewhere. A story about the canteen queue, a visitor badge, and scripts you stop rewriting from scratch.

item.title: One Folder for Freelance Excel Trackers? The Garage Forecourt
item.description: Wednesday, 11:20, a garage forecourt, and a client asking what is outstanding. A story about too many files and the calm of having one place.

item.title: Client Asking for a Discount? How to Reply Without Losing Them
item.description: The email says 'any chance of a better price?' and your stomach drops. A calm story about replying to a discount request without losing the client.

item.title: Client Ghosted Me After the Proposal: What Do I Do? The Tuesday Queue
item.description: You sent the proposal ten days ago and heard nothing. In the supermarket queue you check your phone again. A calm story about the silence, and what eases it.

item.title: Client Keeps Asking for Extra Work for Free? What Do I Say?
item.description: A client slips in 'one more small thing' again. A story about the pause before you answer, and finding words that are kind, clear and still yours.

item.title: Client Keeps Changing the Scope? The Car Wash and the Blank Email
item.description: The client changed the brief again and your reply box is empty. A short story about finding calm words to say no without losing the client.

item.title: Client Ignoring Your Emails? The Recycling Centre Queue
item.description: Third email sent, still silence. In a queue of cars full of glass, you realise the problem isn't the client. It's the blank page. A short story.

item.title: Client Keeps Moving the Deadline? The Email You Dread Writing
item.description: The third 'can we push it a week?' arrives while you're in the bakery queue. Here's how the dreaded deadline email stops feeling like a confrontation.

item.title: Client Paid My Invoice, But Which Hours Did It Cover?
item.description: The payment landed, but you can't tell which hours it covered. A calm story about a Monday-morning bank notification and finally seeing it clearly.

item.title: Client Paid Only Part of My Invoice: The Monday Bank Notification
item.description: The money arrived, but it's not the full amount. Now you can't tell what's still outstanding. A short story about a Monday morning, and the calm after.

item.title: Client Paid the Wrong Amount? The Copy Shop and the 2,000 Mystery
item.description: A payment lands, but it matches nothing. Two invoices, one transfer, a gap you can't explain. A quiet story about knowing what's still owed.

item.title: Client Pushing Back on Your Invoice Amount? The Pharmacy Queue
item.description: The client wrote 'this seems higher than expected.' You're in a pharmacy queue with a phone in your hand. A calm story about finding the words.

item.title: Client Says Invoice Was Already Paid? The Car Park Before the Call
item.description: Your client swears the invoice was paid. Your records say nothing either way. A short story about that knot in your stomach, and what calms it.

item.title: Client Taking Forever to Reply? Following Up Without Pushy
item.description: Your client has gone quiet and every follow-up draft sounds either desperate or cross. A quiet Monday-morning story about finding the calm middle.

item.title: CSV Full of Trailing Spaces and Mixed Dates? The Lunch Break Fix
item.description: Half past twelve, a sandwich going cold, and a CSV where every date looks different. A short story about cleaning exports by hand, and the day it stopped.

item.title: Can't Reply to a Difficult Client Email? The Ironing Board Monday
item.description: The email lands at 7:52 on a Monday. You read it four times and still don't know what to write. A story for freelancers who freeze on hard replies.

item.title: Dreading Year-End Bookkeeping? No Idea Where Your Receipts Are
item.description: A video call that starts late, a reminder you've snoozed since October, and the quiet dread of not knowing where your receipts are. A calmer year-end is possible.

item.title: Dreading Year-End Freelance Paperwork? The Hotel Breakfast Reminder
item.description: A calendar reminder pops up over your hotel coffee: 'Year-end admin.' You feel your stomach drop and have no idea where to start. A short story.
